text:
emma_support: Heads up — ACME (customer) opened a ticket: sudden p99 latency regressions and lots of queued requests. They say it started ~2026-03-15T16:20Z. Request load hasn't changed drastically.
customer_bob: Confirmed. Before patch our p99 was ~300ms, now ~2.2s. We saw increasing `queued` markers in the response payloads and occasional 429s with Retry-After.
oncall-bot: Alert: service=inference-prod region=us-west-2 metric=p99 latency value=2240ms threshold=1000ms incident=INC-224900
mike_sre: Checking infra metrics. Worker pool `wgp-usw2-v2` shows concurrency ~= 98/100 and request queue depth up to 420. GPUs sitting at 18-25% — so not GPU bound. Thread dump shows many goroutines waiting on admission tokens.
emma_support: Customer repro steps attached: curl to /v1/generate with model=redwood-xl, 8k max_tokens, concurrent clients=15. They also said auth tokens rotated yesterday.
ravi_runtime: Two potential leads: 1) admission-control concurrency cap is too low for increased per-request work (longer sequences), 2) tokenization/kv-cache changes in latest runtime patch may lengthen per-request CPU compute and hold worker slots longer.
cs_lead_oliver: Customer is on Dedicated reserved capacity — they'd prefer quick mitigations from our side while we investigate root cause.
mike_sre: Quick checks I ran:
```
# peek queue
curl -s http://sre-metrics/api/pools/wgp-usw2-v2 | jq '.concurrency,.queue_depth'
# result: 98, 420
```
Also saw increased syscall wait time on the accelerator host — but not consistent across hosts.
emma_support: Can we give them an ETA / steps? They're seeing production impact.
ravi_runtime: Immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk):
- temporarily raise pool concurrency limit to 140 (if autoscaler rules allow)
- route a subset of traffic to `wgp-usw2-legacy` (different admission semantics)
- enable short-circuit fast-fail for requests > 6s to avoid long-running queue hold
- rollback the runtime kernel change (last rollout at 2026-03-15T03:12Z)
mike_sre: I'll try increasing concurrency for the pool and add a temporary soft-limit. Doing that now.
mike_sre: Patch applied: set concurrency=140 for wgp-usw2-v2. Also opened a routing rule to spill 20% to wgp-usw2-legacy. Monitoring.
oncall-bot: Deploy: routing-change to wgp-usw2-legacy (spill 20%) by mike_sre at 2026-03-15T16:28Z — status: success
customer_bob: After changes p99 dropped to ~780ms within 3m. Still higher than before but much better. Thanks.
ravi_runtime: Good signal. Next steps to find root cause: capture full request profiles (token length distributions, kv-cache hit/miss, per-request CPU user/sys time) for a 30m window. Also correlate with auth rotation — if clients retry with new tokens we might be seeing brief concurrency bursts.
emma_support: I'll ask ACME for a timeline of their token rotation and whether any clients retried simultaneously.
mike_sre: I'll collect worker-level traces and check for lock contention in admission path. If kernel changes are implicated we can run a quick canary rollback. Also suggest we add a temporary 429 with Retry-After for requests that would stall > 5s to protect the pool.
cs_lead_oliver: Notify customer that we applied temporary mitigations (raised concurrency, spill routing). We're investigating and will follow up with a timeline and next actions.
emma_support: Noted — communicating now. Will post update here when ACME replies with token rotation time.
customer_bob: We rotated tokens at 16:18Z and saw a flurry of retries till 16:24Z, that might align with your spike. Happy with the temporary fixes, want a root-cause and final mitigation.
ravi_runtime: Thanks — that confirms correlated retry burst. We'll keep the spill routing for 2 hours while we dig in. If kernel rollback is needed we'll coordinate a canary and change window.
mike_sre: Monitoring shows queue depth down to ~70 and p99 ~520ms at 16:34Z. Marking this incident as triaged — continuing RCA.
emma_support: Closing loop: customer informed, oncall engaged, temporary mitigations in place. Will update subject line if we schedule rollback or longer-term fixes.
